task.description: Second retry of fn:git-merge per docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md, run_id WF03-ISS0262-20260822, branch feature/WF03-ISS0262-20260822. The prior two Step Final FAILs were both caused by H6's per-file grandfather list being outpaced by concurrently-landing runs; that mechanism has since been REPLACED with a commit-boundary rule (h6_floor_commit/0, pre_floor_file?/2) that automatically grandfathers any non-JSON handoff file that existed before the floor, so a rebase picking up yet another concurrently-merged run's handoff files should no longer trip H6 -- verify this expectation holds for real rather than assuming it. Known, pre-existing, EXPLICITLY OUT-OF-SCOPE finding you will likely still see in mix letflow.lint_handoffs output: an H1/H3 (not H6) violation on handoffs/WF03-ISS0260-20260822/step-04d-test-design-validator-recheck.json, from an unrelated already-merged run, confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to this branch's diff (git diff --stat main...HEAD never touches that path) -- attribute it structurally per GIT_MERGE.md's Precondition section ("green means no failure attributable to this branch") and file it as a new issue rather than blocking on it or fixing it yourself; do not let it stop the merge. If you discover ANY NEW H6 violation (i.e. the floor-commit mechanism itself failed to grandfather a pre-existing file, or a genuinely new post-floor file that should legitimately fail), that IS a real blocker -- stop and report FAIL with full detail, do not attempt to patch the mechanism yourself. Full procedure: fetch origin main, rebase, format/compile/test with structural attribution, push, create PR (prefix 'fix:', title 'fix: lint_handoffs detects non-JSON handoff files via new H6 check [WF03-ISS0262-20260822]'), merge --squash --delete-branch, local cleanup back to main.
